claim: Gros & Devanbu propose localizing where in generated code an LLM's output is likely misaligned with user intent, by assigning a well-calibrated probability to arbitrary code spans indicating the empirical odds that span will be edited in a minimal repair patch.
stance_target: highest title-level scoop-risk match to 'structured/localized code confidence' but distinct structuring axis (spatial/line vs per-test-case)
scope_conditions: code generated by large LLMs, repaired via minimal intent-aligning patches
quoted_support: we offer techniques to localize where generations might be misaligned from user intent... we measure how well various techniques can assign a well-calibrated probability to indicate which parts of code will be edited in a minimal patch (i.e., give a probability that corresponds with empirical odds it is edited).

claim: Ground-truth labels come from a curated 'Minimal Intent Aligning Patches' dataset of repaired programs verified using test cases -- NOT from directly reusing already-computed per-test pass/fail as a free label, since patch construction is itself a dataset-building contribution.
stance_target: distinguishes this paper's label-construction cost from the proposed 'free per-test labels' framing
quoted_support: We first create a dataset of 'Minimal Intent Aligning Patches' of repaired LLM generated programs. Each program uses test cases to verify correctness.

claim: A small white-box supervisor probe on a generator model's internal activations achieves low calibration error and a Brier Skill Score of approximately 0.2 for predicting edited lines, even when probing models many orders of magnitude larger than the probe itself.
stance_target: state-of-the-art localized code-calibration performance as of late 2025
scope_conditions: white-box probing vs black-box reflective/self-consistency baselines
quoted_support: We find probes with a small supervisor model can achieve low calibration error and Brier Skill Score of approx 0.2 estimating edited lines on code generated by models many orders of magnitude larger.

claim: The confidence estimator is an external probe trained on model internals, not the code-generating LLM itself trained via SFT/RL to natively verbalize/express calibrated confidence -- a key mechanistic distinction from the proposed method.
stance_target: distinguishes mechanism (external probe) from the proposed method (native expressed confidence via training)
quoted_support: We compare white-box probing (where we propose a technique for efficient arbitrary-span querying), against black-box reflective and self-consistency based approaches.

claim: A probe trained only on code shows some signs of generalizing to natural-language error localization when new probability scaling is allowed, suggesting the localization mechanism may transfer beyond code.
stance_target: generalizability of localized calibration probes across modalities
scope_conditions: cross-domain generalization test, code-trained probe applied to NL errors
quoted_support: finding a probe trained only on code shows some signs of generalizing to natural language errors if new probability scaling is allowed.
